title: Searching and binary search
summary: Look through items one by one, or, when they are sorted, halve the search each step.

sections.heading: One by one
body: The simple way checks each item in turn. Built-ins do this for you: `indexOf` in JavaScript, `.index` in Python. On a long list it can mean checking every single item.

sections.heading: Halve it each time
body: Think of guessing a number from 1 to 100 when you are told "higher" or "lower". Always guess the middle and you need at most 7 guesses.
Binary search does that on a **sorted** list. Keep `lo` and `hi` around the part still possible, look at the middle, and throw away the half that cannot contain the target.

javascript.code:
const items = [2, 5, 8, 12, 16, 23, 38, 56, 72, 91]
let lo = 0
let hi = items.length - 1
let steps = 0
while (lo <= hi) {
  steps++
  const mid = Math.floor((lo + hi) / 2)
  if (items[mid] === 23) break
  if (items[mid] < 23) lo = mid + 1
  else hi = mid - 1
}
console.log('found in', steps, 'steps')

python.code:
items = [2, 5, 8, 12, 16, 23, 38, 56, 72, 91]
lo = 0
hi = len(items) - 1
steps = 0
while lo <= hi:
    steps += 1
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    if items[mid] == 23:
        break
    if items[mid] < 23:
        lo = mid + 1
    else:
        hi = mid - 1
print('found in', steps, 'steps')

mistakes: Using binary search on a list that is not sorted.
Writing `lo < hi` instead of `lo <= hi` and missing the last remaining item.
In JavaScript, `(lo + hi) / 2` can be a decimal. Wrap it in `Math.floor`.
Setting `lo = mid` instead of `mid + 1`, which can loop forever.
